Now that that's out of my system, let me try putting it to you in terms that most people don't think of.

Cooking is heat transfer.

That's it. You are moving the warmth from your pan or your oven or your whatever and into your food over a period of time. Not enough heat or time and the food's raw; too much heat or time and it's burnt. Learn how your stovetop and oven works. Figure out where low, medium, and high settings are (hint: it's not always where you think it should be by the numbers on the dial or whatever). Learn the in-betweens: medium low and medium high. The beauty is that if things are moving too fast, you can always just turn down the heat a notch or two and just let it cook longer.

Start with simple shit. Breakfast. Scrambled eggs, toast and bacon. Toast cooks itself (as long as you set the toaster to the right setting). Gordon Ramsey has a wonderful video on how to cook scrambled eggs. And 10 seconds before it's burnt, bacon is done crispy and perfect. If you can't handle doing it in a pan, lay out the strips on a piece of parchment paper on a baking sheet and throw it in a 500°F oven until it looks like you like it. Move on to homemade egg mcmuffins - it's literally the same meal, just the shit's stacked up and not sitting next to each other on the plate. Graduate to French Toast. Again, pretty much the same meal, except the scrambled eggs are coating the bread instead of next to it or on top of it.

Learn to vary your ingredients according to your tastes. Try different kinds of bacon, different kinds of cheeses, different kinds of bread. Add a couple drops of vanilla extract to your batter. Maybe a tiny pinch of salt. Graduate again to fresh baked bread from a bakery. Learn what works and what doesn't. French toast made with rye bread would be pretty shitty, but how do you know until you try it?

I have fought this battle and won. First and foremost: eat what you cook, even if it tastes like garbage. Wasting food is a grievous sin, especially when you're just getting started on your own. Furthermore, nothing tells you exactly where you failed like tasting and smelling every single mistake. If what you cooked is still raw, nuke it for a minute or two. If it's charcoal, I'd say that's the only acceptable moment to throw it out. Otherwise just scrape off the burnt outer layer and eat what's inside.

Herbs and spices: Most basic, simple, easy recipes never need more than three of each. Of you're following a recipe or have a specific dish in mind, for fuck's sake THINK about the meal. Cumin does not go with Italian cuisine (usually). Parsley has almost no place in Mexican food. Understanding the culture behind the meal helps you MAKE the god damned meal.

Meat: DO NOT take a frozen slab of meat and slap ot straight onto the heat. The outside will burn before the inside is even close to done. THAW OUT YOUR GOD DAMNED MEAT. Yes, it takes fucking time. Sometimes, all you need to do is leave it in a bowl of warm water for an hour or so. Sometimes it's better to just pop it in the fridge before you leave for work in the morning. Even if it's just "mostly" thawed, you will still get infinitely better results than if you try to go straight from frozen to cooked.

Vegetables: Aside from onions and garlic, if vegetables are anything other than a vibrant shade of their original color, you have probably overcooked them. Root vegetables have a significant bit more wiggle room in this field, but otherwise, when it comes to veggies, cooking them fast and quick is better than cooking them into mush.
